name: CagriSema
lead: CagriSema is an investigational once-weekly injectable combination of cagrilintide, an amylin receptor agonist, and semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, developed by Novo Nordisk for weight management [1][4]. It is intended for adults with overweight or obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes, and is not an appearance product in itself; any effect on looks comes through fat loss.

In a phase 3a trial in adults without diabetes, the combination produced a mean body-weight change of about 20% over 68 weeks versus about 3% with placebo [1][7]. A meta-analysis of three early randomized trials found greater weight loss with the combination than with semaglutide 2.4 mg alone, together with more gastrointestinal adverse events [4]. In a head-to-head open-label trial reported by the developer, it did not meet the non-inferiority endpoint against tirzepatide [1].

Per Grokipedia, a new drug application was filed with the US FDA in December 2025, and the product was not approved at the time of that source [1]. In forum discussion, CagriSema is mentioned alongside other newer peptides such as retatrutide [15].
infobox: Amylin receptor agonist + GLP-1 receptor agonist (fixed combination)

paras: The studied use is chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or with overweight plus a weight-related condition, with or without type 2 diabetes [1][7][8]. Separate phase 3 programs have also examined its effects on blood glucose in type 2 diabetes and on blood pressure [10][11][12]. Registered trials include studies in adolescents with type 2 diabetes, people with hypertension and obesity, and weight-loss maintenance [16][17][18].

A phase 2 trial in type 2 diabetes tested the coadministration of cagrilintide 2.4 mg and semaglutide 2.4 mg against each agent alone [9]. In the 68-week phase 3a REDEFINE 1 trial in adults with overweight or obesity, CagriSema was compared with placebo and with each component alone [7]. Grokipedia reports a change of -20.4% versus -3.0% with placebo, and about 80% of participants with gastrointestinal adverse events [1]. A companion trial in adults with type 2 diabetes (REDEFINE 2) is reported there to have shown smaller weight reductions, around 15.7% versus 3.1% on placebo [8][1]. A blood-pressure analysis of REDEFINE 1 has also been published [11].

A 2024 meta-analysis of three randomized trials with 430 participants reported a mean difference of about -9 percentage points in weight versus semaglutide 2.4 mg at 20-32 weeks, with high heterogeneity; gastrointestinal events and vomiting were higher with the combination [4]. Phase 3 REIMAGINE trials in type 2 diabetes have been published in 2026 [10][12]. Recent network meta-analyses and reviews place CagriSema among next-generation obesity drugs expected to achieve weight loss in the range of tirzepatide [2][3][5][6][13].

In the REDEFINE 4 open-label head-to-head trial against tirzepatide 15 mg, as reported by Grokipedia, weight loss was 20.2% to 23.0% with CagriSema versus 23.6% to 25.5% with tirzepatide, and non-inferiority was not met [1]. Ongoing registered trials include a 2,500-person phase 3 study and a trial of switching from semaglutide [19][20].

The reported adverse-event profile resembles that of the GLP-1 class: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation, mostly mild to moderate [1][4]. Grokipedia reports about 6% discontinuation for adverse events and injection-site reactions in about 12% of users [1]. Since the product is unapproved, no official label or contraindication list exists.

Semaglutide activates GLP-1 receptors and cagrilintide acts on amylin receptors; amylin is a hormone co-secreted with insulin that influences satiety and postprandial glucose [14][6]. Reviews describe combining hormones with complementary actions as a strategy to increase weight loss beyond GLP-1 agonism alone [3][5]. Grokipedia reports a 16-week dose-escalation period [1].

Because CagriSema is unapproved, any use outside trials would be of unregulated product. Posts in a T Nation thread group it with retatrutide and other research peptides that users describe positively [15]. Regulators have not authorized it for sale.

lore.intro: CagriSema appears only briefly in community discussion, usually as an upcoming or research-grade successor to semaglutide, listed beside retatrutide [15].

claims.claim: CagriSema "kicks ass" for fat loss alongside retatrutide
claims.believers: A forum poster lists CagriSema with retatrutide among compounds they rate highly [15].
claims.experts: Phase 3 trials report roughly 20% weight loss at 68 weeks in adults without diabetes, and published reviews expect weight loss comparable to tirzepatide, though it was reported as not non-inferior to tirzepatide in one open-label trial [7][5][1].

card.summary: Not-yet-approved weekly semaglutide plus cagrilintide shot that cut weight about 20% in phase 3 trials.
card.note: Investigational; unapproved supply is unregulated. GI side effects common.

quick.overview:
CagriSema is a once-weekly injection that pairs semaglutide with cagrilintide, an amylin analogue. It is being developed by Novo Nordisk for obesity and type 2 diabetes.

Phase 3 trials report about 20% mean weight loss over 68 weeks in adults without diabetes, more than semaglutide alone but less than tirzepatide in one head-to-head comparison.
quick.mechanism: Semaglutide activates GLP-1 receptors and cagrilintide activates amylin receptors; both reduce appetite and slow eating, through partly different pathways.
quick.risks: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation are the most reported effects, and were more frequent than with semaglutide alone. It is an investigational drug without an approved label; any supply outside trials is unregulated.
